meta.title: The lazy path, end to end
meta.note: NOTHING LOADS THIS AT BOOT, and that is the point of it. It is a second package: fetched on demand through import.meta.glob (its own content-hashed chunk, see src/content/storage/bundled.ts), declaring a dependency on `core`, and holding one quest that REFERENCES content core shipped — npc:gain and town:encampment. So it exercises every part of the design the core package cannot: a dependency resolved before the referring assets are read, a cross-package reference that the graph must resolve rather than report as dangling, a lease that can be dropped, and an unload that takes the definitions away while leaving the player's flags and quest statuses exactly where they are (spec §12.3).
meta.text-is-inline: Its strings are the { text } form rather than { key }, which is the OTHER half of ContentText being demonstrated: StringKey is a build-time guarantee and content authored outside the build cannot have it, so a package like this carries its words with it and falls back across languages the way t() does. Nothing in src/i18n/ has to know this package exists.
meta.loading-it: content.load('example-quest', 'quest'), and content.release('example-quest', 'quest') to put it back.

text.en: Someone in the Encampment has been waiting for a word with you.
